column4: Visit note | 2025-09-17 10:30 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Rezaul Bepari, 48, male. Mr. Bepari reports suffering from intense nausea, needing to lie in a dark room, and a throbbing headache on one side of his head. He mentions that these episodes have been worse since starting night shifts at a hospital in Gulshan, occurring about 12 headache days a month. He works as a fisherman. He reports no relevant medical comorbidities. On examination, his blood pressure is 118/70 mmHg, pulse is 90 bpm, and weight is 84 kg. Cranial nerves are intact and neurological exam is otherwise normal. Assessment: Migraine. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to keep a headache diary, sleep and eat at regular times, and limit screen time. Follow-up is scheduled in 3 months with the headache diary.

Visit note | 2025-09-24 10:00 AM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Mahmuda Bhuiyan, 26, female. Ms. Bhuiyan presents because she has been missing work or classes due to severe pain, painful cramps in the first days of each period, and associated nausea with the pain. She notes that her symptoms are worse since starting a job with long standing hours in Sirajganj, with a pain score 6/10, spreading to the lower back and thighs with vomiting. She has no chronic comorbidities. On examination, her vitals show BP 132/82 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, and weight 55 kg. Abdominal examination reveals mild tenderness with no palpable masses. Assessment: Primary dysmenorrhoea. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to use a hot water bottle, do light exercise, and keep a period diary. Follow-up in 3 months with the period diary.

Visit note | 2025-09-24 12:00 PM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Hafiz Mahmud, 53, male. Mr. Mahmud states he has been scratching at night, noting his symptoms are worse in winter, along with itchy dry patches on the elbows and knees. He explains it has been worse since switching to a strong detergent in Jashore, with the affected area about 3 cm across. He works as a sales representative and has no other major illnesses. Examination reveals dry, erythematous skin plaques on both elbows and knees; other vitals are BP 136/71 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm, and weight 48 kg. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to use a mild soap, avoid hot baths, and wear cotton clothes. Follow-up is in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-10-01 11:30 AM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Sakib Kabir, 44, male. Mr. Kabir comes in looking pale, getting breathless on the stairs, and feeling in a state of constant tiredness. He mentions his condition worsened after a long spell of poor meals while living alone in Badda. He works as a schoolteacher and has no known comorbidity. He also mentions experiencing a craving to chew ice and a sore smooth tongue with little tiredness. On physical examination, his haemoglobin is 10.3 g/dL, BP is 120/75 mmHg, pulse is 82 bpm, and weight is 93 kg. Conjunctivae are pale. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and to avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.

Visit note | 2025-10-01 03:00 PM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Farhan Akand, 62, male. Mr. Akand complains of stiffness in the morning for a few minutes, knee pain on the stairs, and a creaking knee. He notes his discomfort is worse after a long sightseeing trip on foot in Chattogram, with a BMI 32.2. He works as a textile engineer and has no significant past medical history. He reports an episode of sudden locking of the knee with little pain. Examination of the lower limbs reveals crepitus and mild restriction in flexion; vitals show BP 130/74 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, weight 87 kg. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up in 6 weeks with physiotherapy.

Visit note | 2025-10-04 09:00 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Sultana Pramanik, 30, female. Ms. Pramanik reports concerns regarding weight gain, acne, and irregular periods. She states her symptoms were noticed after a friend in Shyamoli suggested testing, and her examination records a BMI 32.7. She works as a bank officer and has no underlying comorbidities. General and systemic examinations are unremarkable; vitals are BP 128/76 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, and weight 58 kg. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment, including a pelvic ultrasound and hormone profile; no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to aim for 5 percent weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-10-04 09:30 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Iffat Molla, 23, female. Ms. Molla presents with marks left after pimples, persistent pimples and blackheads on the face, and spots on the back. She shares that her condition is worse since working in a hot kitchen in Tangail, noting about 13 inflamed spots on the face. She works as an accountant and has a comorbidity of Essential hypertension. On examination, her blood pressure is 140/92 mmHg, pulse is 88 bpm, and weight is 67 kg. Skin examination shows multiple papules and comedones. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests; no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and do not squeeze spots. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-10-04 10:00 AM | Dr. Shamima Nasrin, Ophthalmology | Patient: Shapla Akand, 75, female. Mrs. Akand describes symptoms that are worse in air conditioning, along with gritty burning eyes, and long hours of screen time. She states it became worse since night shifts at a call centre in Kushtia, with a tear break-up time 7 seconds. She works as a farmer and has a comorbidity of Hypothyroidism. On examination, her visual acuity is stable, conjunctiva are slightly injected, vitals record BP 112/80 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, and weight 78 kg. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: a tear film break-up test; no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-10-04 10:30 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Rashid Gazi, 64, male. Mr. Gazi reports experiencing numbness in his toes, with symptoms that are worse at night, alongside a burning sensation in both feet. He mentions this started after years of high sugar found at a health camp in Gulshan, showing reduced sensation at 8 of 10 monofilament test sites. He works as a tailor and has no other major comorbidity. Neurological examination confirms distal sensory loss in both lower extremities; other vitals are BP 127/83 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, weight 58 kg. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to check the feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-10-05 02:30 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Ratan Roy, 65, male. Mr. Roy complains of knee pain on the stairs and stiffness in the morning for a few minutes. He notes it is worse after a long sightseeing trip on foot in Gulshan, with a BMI 33.1. He is a retired civil servant and has no reported comorbidity. Musculoskeletal examination shows bilateral crepitus and tenderness around the patella; vitals show BP 110/79 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, and weight 81 kg. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: a knee X-ray; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up after the test results are ready.
